frequency_question: How often does institutional and structural friction successfully prevent an initiated policy tightening within the defined window?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign central bank tightening episodes in major emerging markets (e.g., India, Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa) since 1995 where structural friction (e.g., statutory government consultations, board vetoes, or direct ministry pushback) was formally present; excludes voluntary pauses driven purely by endogenous economic data without structural intervention.

cases.name: RBI rate hike cycle (Urjit Patel era pushback)
Banco Central do Brasil political pressure episode
South African Reserve Bank mandate pushback
Bank of Mexico board split intervention

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named prominent episodes; universe of emerging market central bank resistance episodes is estimated around 25, but structural failure to hike due solely to institutional friction rather than macro data is extremely rare.
known_gaps: Excludes minor unpublicized ministerial disagreements that did not reach formal policy meeting stages.
skeleton: Total recorded emerging market central bank tightening cycles with formal structural friction attempts vs. instances where the friction successfully prevented the hike.
multiplier: 6 observed institutional friction attempts / 0 successful structural blocks resulting in cancellation of the initiated hike within the cycle window.
validity_reason: Institutional autonomy frameworks for major emerging market central banks remain stable over medium-term horizons.
